summary: This week we featured research on job search, public procurement, tax collection and more!

title: Making tax collection cheaper could unlock growth
summary: Low-income countries collect as little as $30 in tax for every dollar they spend collecting it. High-income countries collect $270. New research suggests that improving the efficiency of how taxes are collected could significantly lift the GDP of low-income countries.

title: How centralised procurement cuts drug prices and pharmaceutical marketing
summary: In China, guaranteeing auction winners a fixed share of public hospital purchases cut generic drug prices by around 40% and led winning firms to spend less on marketing, showing that procurement design can curb costly competition for prescriptions where hidden payments are diffi…

title: How digital monitoring gets tractors to the most productive farms
summary: In tractor rental markets, owners who cannot observe their operators keep machines close to home, leaving farmers in more productive, remote areas without access to mechanisation. Evidence from around 1,200 GPS-tracked tractors in Kenya shows that digital monitoring expands thei…

title: Can correcting misconceptions about therapy help students seek care?
summary: Evidence from a survey experiment in Mexico shows that correcting misconceptions about therapy makes university students more likely to share counselling information with peers, while raising therapy use only among students who had recently used it.

title: Implementation science in education: Scaling what works
summary: Around 70% of children in low- and middle-income countries cannot read a simple text, even though cost-effective approaches such as structured pedagogy and teaching at the right level are well evidenced. A four-stage framework – efficacy trials, effectiveness trials, policy plan…

title: When cheaper job ads lead to harder-to-fill jobs
summary: In Ethiopia, subsidising vacancy-posting costs leads small and medium-sized enterprises to advertise publicly and create more white-collar positions, which they then struggle to fill.

title: Public roads on private land: How land acquisition costs shape where cities should build roads
summary: Evidence from 114 km of road upgrades in Kampala shows that the cost of acquiring land is decisive both for the net returns to urban road improvements and for where they are optimally built. When public funds are scarce, requiring full compensation to protect landowners need not…

title: Transmission losses drive electricity productivity gaps
summary: Productivity in the electricity sector of low-income countries is far closer to the global frontier than economy-wide productivity, and because power is a strong complement to other inputs, raising it to the frontier would lift GDP by less than 1.2% on average – evidence that el…

title: Weak property rights and lax enforcement fuel tropical forest fires
summary: Indonesian firms burn more forest land when the fire spread risk falls on unclaimed land. Clearer property rights and credible penalties could cut fires by half.

title: How to fund social insurance without pushing workers into informality
summary: Stronger collection of social insurance contributions in China reduced formal firm entry and shifted workers towards informal jobs.

title: Critical minerals scramble: Turning a windfall into development
summary: The global scramble for critical minerals offers resource-rich economies a large but possibly short-lived windfall – one that well-designed contracts, royalties and industrial policy can turn into lasting development rather than another resource curse.

title: Can we detect when a country's institutions are about to change?
summary: Using AI to analyse 120 years of newspaper coverage produces a new index of uncertainty about a country's core institutions, and in the countries studied, nearly every major shift in democracy happened when this index was high. Because it detects slow-building uncertainty that o…

title: Can role models uplift marginalised communities?
summary: In Vietnam, a low-cost video intervention featuring successful entrepreneurs briefly raised ethnic minority farmers' belief in their own agency. However, it did not raise household incomes, and for households hit by natural disasters it may have made things worse.

title: Ocean acidification is raising newborn deaths in coastal communities
summary: Rising ocean acidity cuts small-scale fish catches, pushes up seafood prices and worsens women's nutrition, increasing neonatal mortality in coastal communities of low- and middle-income countries by around 5% for each 0.01-unit fall in pH. Cutting emissions, limiting industrial…

title: Mining booms move workers from farms to services, not factories
summary: Global evidence from 2,041 cities linked to 33,262 mines producing 23 minerals shows that resource booms reshape local employment patterns far more than they drive urbanisation.
